title: How Garry Tan builds an AI-native software factory with skills, resolvers and evals
summary: Garry Tan explains how coding agents let one founder do the work of hundreds, and the primitives he uses: skills, resolvers, skillify, tests and a memory brain. He stresses pairing deterministic code with latent-space agents, and judging results by whether customers actually pay.

principles.text: Stop avoiding big scope: with coding agents one person can attempt work that used to need hundreds.
principles.quote: my response to that, based on my experience with uh coding agents and what's happening right now, is actually let's boil the ocean.

principles.text: Agent failures usually come from mixing deterministic work and latent-space work; put each in the right layer.
principles.quote: you need to make the latent space work with the deterministic space.

principles.text: Use a resolver instead of a bloated instruction file: load instructions only when a task needs them.
principles.quote: anytime you have to write to the change log, load change log.md.

principles.text: Once an agent task works, skillify it, but writing the skill and code is only a small part; tests and evals make it reliable.
principles.quote: Writing the skill and writing the code is only two out of the 10 steps.

principles.text: Avoid shipping AI slop by driving test coverage to 80-90% with an engineering review step.
principles.quote: to get to 80-90% test coverage so that I am not shipping slop.

principles.text: Judge output by real-world results: does it work for customers and are they paying, not lines of code.
principles.quote: Does it work for your customers? Are people actually paying? That's actually the true metric.
